title: 19. Volume and Surface Areas of Solids

q.t: Find the volume of a cube of side 4 cm.
Find the volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the volume of a cone of radius 7 cm and height 12 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: A cone holds ⅓ of the cylinder on the same base and height: ⅓ × 154 × 12.

q.t: Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the curved surface area of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Unroll it into a rectangle: circumference 44 × height 10.

q.t: A cone has radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. Find its slant height.
q.e: Radius, height and slant height make a right triangle: √(36 + 64).

q.t: Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: S = 4πr² — four times the area of its biggest circle.

q.t: Find the volume of a 5 cm × 4 cm × 3 cm cuboid.
Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Curved part 2πr² plus the flat circle πr²: 3πr².

q.t: Find the curved surface area of a cone of radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
A metal sphere of radius 3 cm is melted into a cylinder of radius 2 cm. Find the cylinder’s height.
q.e: Volume stays the same: (4/3)π × 27 = π × 4 × h, so 36 = 4h.

q.t: A toy is a cone of radius 7 cm and height 24 cm on a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its total surface area. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Slant height = 25. Outside surface = cone’s πrl + hemisphere’s 2πr² = 550 + 308.

q.t: How many balls of radius 1 cm can be made by melting a ball of radius 3 cm?
A cylinder and a cone have the same base and height. Find volume of cylinder : volume of cone.
q.e: A cone holds exactly one-third of the matching cylinder.

q.t: Cubes of sides 3, 4 and 5 cm are melted into one cube. Find its side.
Two cubes of volume 64 cm³ each are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the cuboid.
q.e: Each cube has side 4, so the cuboid is 8 × 4 × 4: 2(32 + 32 + 16).

q.t: A hemispherical bowl has radius 10.5 cm. Find its inner curved surface area. (π = 22/7)
A frustum of a cone has end radii 10 cm and 4 cm and height 21 cm. Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
A well of diameter 7 m is dug 20 m deep. Find the volume of earth taken out. (π = 22/7)
Two spheres have radii in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the ratio of their volumes.
A cylindrical bucket of radius 8 cm and height 21 cm is full of sand. It is emptied into a conical heap 28 cm high. Find the heap’s radius.
A frustum has end radii 14 cm and 7 cm and slant height 10 cm. Find its curved surface area. (π = 22/7)
Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of inner radius 3.5 cm. How many litres flow in 1 minute? (π = 22/7)
q.e: Each second a 200 cm long cylinder flows out: 38.5 × 200 = 7700 cm³. In 60 s: 462000 cm³.

q.t: A capsule is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. It is 20 cm long with diameter 6 cm. Find its surface area. (π = 22/7)
A cone of the same radius (7 cm) and height (24 cm) is hollowed out of a solid cylinder. Find the volume left. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Cylinder 3696 minus cone ⅓ of it: ⅔ × 3696.

q.t: A hollow sphere has outer radius 5 cm and inner radius 3 cm. It is melted into a cone of base radius 4 cm. Find the cone’s height.
A bucket is a frustum with end radii 20 cm and 10 cm and height 21 cm. How many litres does it hold? (π = 22/7)
A copper rod of radius 1 cm and length 24 cm is drawn into a wire 96 m long. Find the wire’s diameter in mm.
q.e: π × 1 × 24 = π r² × 9600, so r² = 1/400 and r = 0.05 cm. Diameter 0.1 cm.

q.t: A cone is cut halfway up its height, parallel to the base. Find volume of small cone : volume of frustum.
q.e: The small cone is half as big in every length, so 1/8 of the volume. The frustum is the other 7/8.

q.t: How many litres does a 4 m × 3 m × 2 m tank hold?
A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 3 m with a cone of slant height 10 m on top. Canvas costs ₹50 per m². Find the cost of canvas (in ₹). (π = 22/7)
A well 14 m across is dug 15 m deep. The earth is spread evenly in a 7 m wide ring around it. How high is the ring? (π = 22/7)
q.e: Earth = π × 49 × 15. The ring runs from radius 7 to 14: area π(196 − 49) = 147π. Height = 735π ÷ 147π.

q.t: A bucket open at the top is a frustum with radii 20 cm and 8 cm and height 16 cm. Find the metal needed. (π = 22/7)
q.e: Slant = √(256 + 144) = 20. Metal = π(R + r)l + πr² (the bottom only) = π(560 + 64).

q.t: Marbles of diameter 1.4 cm are dropped into a cylindrical beaker of radius 3.5 cm. How many raise the water by 5.6 cm?
A cone of radius 6 cm and height 24 cm is melted into a sphere. Find its radius.
A solid is a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm topped by a hemisphere of radius 7 cm. Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
Water flows at 10 km/h through a pipe of diameter 14 cm into a 40 m × 22 m tank. How many hours until the water rises 35 cm? (π = 22/7)
A hemispherical bowl of radius 9 cm is full of liquid. It is poured into bottles that are cylinders of diameter 3 cm and height 4 cm. How many bottles are filled?
A cone 30 cm high is cut parallel to its base so that the small cone on top has 1/27 of the volume. How high above the base is the cut?
q.e: Volume ratio 1/27 means length ratio 1/3, so the small cone is 10 cm tall. 30 − 10.

q.t: A solid hemisphere has total surface area 462 cm². Find its volume. (π = 22/7)
